title: Higher LNG prices, supply shortages compound Bangladesh gas crisis
content:
The deepening gas and electricity crises in Bangladesh have been compounded by a sharp rise in global LNG prices and supply shortages coinciding with high power demand. 
Industrial production has been severely hit, with 70 per cent of the production capacity of gas-dependent factories staying unutilised, pressuring the export sector. 
The energy crunch is no longer confined to power-intensive industries.

title: Can Bangladesh’s fiscal reset put growth on a faster track?
content:
Bangladesh is set to shift its fiscal year from July-June to April-March, with FY2027-28 a nine-month transition before April 2028. 
A five-member committee will identify constitutional, legal and financial-system changes needed to implement the calendar. 
An April start could create a three-month dry-season window for faster construction, but experts warn old bottlenecks may persist.

title: Cambodia’s ASEAN apparel exports rise but trail Asia-Pacific growth
content:
Cambodia’s apparel exports to ASEAN rose 5.5 per cent to $157.242 million in H1 2026.
Growth outpaced the 2.1 per cent rise in worldwide apparel exports but trailed Asia-Pacific’s 6.8 per cent expansion.
ASEAN held 10.4 per cent of Cambodia’s Asia-Pacific apparel exports and nearly 1.7 per cent of worldwide shipments.
T-shirts, jerseys and coats grew; trousers, shorts and shirts declined.
